title: fix(console): a `file` field on a FormView renders the shared upload control, not a text box
body:
Fixes #10167

`Clause-②: no` — declared on the claim, unchanged on delivery. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over this branch's three paths prints `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched`. `apps/console` is an application, not a published contract face, and this repair pulls an outlier back to an already-declared field type rather than widening any accepted set.

Seat session, in prose because footers do not survive an edit: `session_01Xr7APep6jm1Zta3KUzPzZf`.

## Premise, re-taken on `origin/main` `98178b2`

The switch is `FieldInput`'s `switch (field.type)` in `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx`. Parsed out of the switch body rather than read by eye, its arms before this branch were, in tree order — 21 of them:

`textarea` · `paragraph` · `long_text` · `number` · `integer` · `decimal` · `currency` · `email` · `url` · `password` · `date` · `time` · `datetime` · `timestamp` · `boolean` · `toggle` · `checkbox` · `select` · `picklist` · `enum` · `radio`

No `file`, so the field fell through to the `default` arm's plain text input. **The card's premise holds.** The same parse answers the dispatch's assumption D: the switch body contains **no** map, lookup table or nested helper — every arm is a literal `case`, so an arm-list reading under-reports nothing *on the type axis*. It under-reports on three other axes; see step 1 below.

## The fix — one arm, and no second file control

The `file` arm asks ADR-0059's resolver (`resolveFormWidgetType` + `getLazyFieldWidget` in `@object-ui/fields`) for the same widget the record form renders. That resolver's own docblock names this the door for a host rendering field widgets outside the form renderer, "so their type support can never drift behind the form surface", and `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `ActionParamDialog` is already on it.

Writing an `input type="file"` here instead would have been a second upload pipeline: a second size guard, a second progress surface, and — the part that actually breaks — a second answer to what a submitted file VALUE is. A hand-rolled control puts a raw `File` into the form's values and the engine answers `expected string, received object`, which is exactly the shape objectui#10131 measured. Through the shared widget, this route submits what the other renderer submits: the `sys_file` id the upload adapter minted, or the legacy inline blob when the adapter surfaced none.

The resolution is hoisted to module scope. `react-hooks/static-components` refuses a component value produced during render, and the arm pins the type at `'file'` anyway, so there is nothing per-render to resolve; `React.lazy` still defers the chunk until the arm first renders.

## Two halves the symptom does not name, and why they are not scope creep

**The object's declared upload configuration now reaches the widget.** This app's local `ObjectFieldDef` admitted no `multiple`, no `accept`, no `maxSize` — all three of which `@objectstack/spec` declares on a field and the server serves. Without them the control would be a single-file, unfiltered, unbounded dropzone whatever the author wrote: declared but not delivered. That is the identical shape objectui#5627 recorded **in this same file** for the conditional rules — "nothing downstream could read a key this file's payload types did not admit".

**Submit is blocked while an upload is in flight.** The widget contract says outright what `onUploadingChange` is for: upload widgets fire it "so a host can block submit until a presigned upload settles". A file's value only becomes an id once the adapter resolves, so a submit that beats it stores nothing for the field and still reports success. Ablation leg C below shows the guard is load-bearing and nothing else depends on it.

## Step 1 — the enumeration this card asked for

The full table is in the `os-dev-report` comment on objectui#10167. Headline, measured — population is `@objectstack/spec/data`'s own `FieldType` enum (49 members), the resolver column is a runtime read of the built `@object-ui/fields`, and the arm column is parsed from the switch:

- **35** of the 49 spec field types resolve to a dedicated widget on the shared resolver and have no arm here. One of those, `text`, is correctly served by the `default` arm; for the other **34** the default text input is the wrong control.
- **0** types are unhandled on both sides. There is no "neither side supports it" bucket: every gap in this switch is a gap against a control that already exists.
- **8** arms here spell names that are not spec `FieldType` members at all (`paragraph`, `long_text`, `integer`, `decimal`, `timestamp`, `checkbox`, `picklist`, `enum`) — a private alias table maintained nowhere else.

⭐ **Three dispatch axes an arm list cannot see, and they are why "add the missing arms" would not close the class:**

1. **`widget`.** The spec declares `widget` as an optional string on a field, and the shared chain reads it (`sectionFields.ts` carries `fd.widget`; `form.tsx` resolves `f?.widget || f?.field?.widget || f?.type`). Three widget keys — `object-ref`, `filter-condition`, `recipient-picker` — are reachable *only* that way. `FormPage` reads no `widget` key anywhere, so it is blind to this axis no matter how many `type` arms it gains.
2. **Arity.** `mapFieldTypeToFormType('select', { multiple: true })` returns `field:multiselect` — a different component. This switch's `select` arm renders a single-value `select` element, so a declared multi-value picklist silently degrades here even though `select` "has an arm".
3. **Retirement.** `resolveFormWidgetType('owner')` returns `owner`, which the registry answers with a tombstone that refuses visibly — the whole point of objectui#4814. Here `owner` has no arm and the default renders a working text box, which is precisely the silent degradation the tombstone exists to prevent.

⛔ Nothing above is acted on in this pull request. Per triage it is evidence for the separate decision-box card about whether this renderer should hold a switch at all.

## Reverse verification — three legs, direction predicted before each run

Run from the committed tree; each mutation is proven on disk before the run (anchor removed, marker injected) and each restore is proven by blob hash against `HEAD` plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| leg | mutation | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | the `file` arm removed — the card's own fix reverted | all six red | 6 failed of 6 |
| B | the row stops carrying `multiple` / `accept` / `maxSize` | exactly the two declaration tests red | 2 failed, 4 passed of 6 |
| C | the `onUploadingChange` signal dropped | exactly the in-flight test red | 1 failed, 5 passed of 6 |

B and C are the discriminating legs: they show the two supporting halves each have their own pin, and that neither pin is carried by the arm.

## Acceptance notes

Observations recorded rather than filed — ⛔ no cards were opened from this seat.

- **noted, not filed:** the required marker in this file is a bare `*` span beside the label, not `aria-hidden`. `ActionParamDialog` hides its own, citing objectui#3299, so that the asterisk stays out of the control's accessible name. Both renderers draw the marker; only one keeps it out of the name. Carrier: whoever next touches this file's label block.
- **noted, not filed, and NOT MEASURED:** `/f/:slug` is the anonymous route, and the console's upload adapter runs the authenticated presign/complete protocol. Whether an anonymous visitor may presign is a backend question this seat could not answer from this checkout — the storage service is not in it. The probe is a real anonymous submit of a form with a `file` field against a running backend. Before this branch the question could not arise, because the control did not exist.
- **noted, not filed:** the three arms this switch spells for numbers (`integer`, `decimal`, plus `currency`) all render the same bare `input type="number"`, while the shared resolver gives `currency` its own widget. Part of the enumeration above, not a separate finding.
